title: Motion Pricing 2026: Plans, Per-Seat Cost, Features
summary: Motion pricing offers Pro AI and Business AI plans billed per seat. See the actual per-seat costs and how they compare to rival tools.
body_markdown:
## Connecting Motion to the rest of your stack with Activepieces


Activepieces is worth adding only if Motion's own integrations leave a manual copy-and-paste step in your process, and it does nothing to replace Motion's scheduling. That distinction keeps this from becoming one more subscription you pay for per seat and then forget to cancel.


### What Motion connects to natively


Start by listing what your team does outside Motion and checking each item against Motion's own integrations list. Calendar sync is the core of the product, and it's the connection you would be paying Motion for anyway.


If your intake, billing and project tracking all live in tools Motion already talks to, there's no gap, and an automation layer is a second bill with nothing to show for it.


Do this check before the trial ends, with the same discipline as the seat count. Every connection you rely on should be one you've seen work on your own data, not one you read about on a feature page.


### Where a workflow tool fills the gap


The gap usually shows up at the edge: a form submission, a CRM deal changing stage, a signed contract.


Someone has to turn that event into a task, and if no native connection does it, a person does it by hand and the cost is their time.


Activepieces handles that hand-off across its 750 integrations, and it keeps unlimited flows on every plan, including the free one. The flow below is a client onboarding example. A Typeform submission triggers it, an agent step runs, and an Asana task is created.


On the right, the trigger is selected, and it asks for a connection and a form. It also offers a test run and mock data, so you can see the trigger fire before you publish anything.


The yellow warning icon on that trigger shows it's not fully configured yet, so the flow wouldn't run as it stands.


The takeaway is the shape, not the tools: an event arrives, a step interprets it, and a task appears somewhere.


You would swap the destination for Motion where a connection to it is available, and you should confirm that in the builder before relying on it.


What follows from this is a pricing question. Treat any automation as another line in your cost model, and price it against the hours it saves.
